objective: Prove that at every n = 2^m >= 4 the corner's return series in the box is 1/(1 + L(w^4)), L(z) = z + z^2 + z^4 + ... + z^n the trace polynomial of GF(2n); on the way, the doubling relation 1/r_2n(w) = 1/r_n(w^2) + w^4 between the sides n and 2n, and at every side n >= 3 the first deviation from the quadrant: the box's first-return series is the quadrant's plus w^(8n) plus higher terms.
status: Obstructed 2026-11-10 (pre-registered in a5769c7a7; refereed): C1, the box law 1/(1 + L(w^4)), not proved for every m but proved at each power of two from 4 to 512 by exact computation (agreement on as many terms as the two recurrence orders together). Reduced by proof (Theorem 7, the two-sided column decomposition; Proposition 8, explicit blocks at a power of two) to one finite identity per side. Proposition 9: det(I + zP_n^o) = 1 + L(z), so the corner returns every four steps as the loop end of a looped path of n sites, a quotient of its orbit. Corollary 10 writes the count of B137 over the same block inverse. Computed: C2 at 4 to 512, C3 to 128, the four-corner formula to 128, the orbit periods to 128.
title: The box law at every power of two
